standard_prerequisites.name: Strict morphisms of filtered objects
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the definition of a strict morphism of filtered objects
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the condition on the induced filtration of the image of a morphism that all three assertions are about.

standard_prerequisites.name: Induced and quotient filtrations are strict
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies that the inclusion and the quotient used in the counterexample are strict morphisms of filtered objects, so that the counterexample really lies inside the hypotheses of part (1).

core_obligations: Part (1) (proof lines 5046-5054): on the two-dimensional vector space B with basis e_1, e_2 filtered by F^n B = B for n < 0, F^0 B = k e_1 and F^n B = 0 for n > 0, the author takes A = k(e_1 + e_2) and C = B/k e_2 with the filtrations induced by B, which are strict by the cited lemma; the composite A -> C is nonzero while the filtration steps force F^n(A) = A for n < 0 and 0 for n at least 0 and F^n(C) = C for n at most 0 and 0 for n > 0, so it is not strict.

Part (2) (proof lines 5056-5066): for injective g the displayed chain of four equalities computes g(f(F^p A)) as (g f)(A) intersected with F^p C, using strictness of f, injectivity of g, strictness of g and the inclusion (g f)(A) contained in g(B).

Part (3) (proof lines 5068-5077): for surjective f the displayed chain of four equalities computes (g f)^{-1}(F^i C) as F^i A + ker(g f), using strictness of g, surjectivity of f, strictness of f and the inclusion ker(f) contained in ker(g f).
proof_roadmap: Build a counterexample on a filtered two-dimensional vector space using induced filtrations.
Compute the image of a filtration step under an injective second map.
Compute the preimage of a filtration step under a surjective first map.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that the composite of two strict morphisms of filtered objects is not strict in general, but is strict when the second map is injective or the first is surjective (statement lines 5034-5043). The proof is a complete argument: part (1) is a concrete counterexample on a filtered two-dimensional vector space, with the induced filtrations verified to be strict through the cited lemma (proof lines 5046-5054); parts (2) and (3) are displayed computations of the image and of the preimage of a filtration step, using strictness and the injectivity or surjectivity hypothesis in each line (proof lines 5056-5077). The non-formal content is the construction of the counterexample. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.
